problems: If the bug made it into a released version, a short entry about fixing `atoms()` on `And`/`Or` with `evaluate=False` would be useful, but the linked issue shows it was a regression found in a release candidate.

The entry says the bug only happened when the arguments came from an iterator or generator. In fact `LatticeOp.__new__` itself turned the arguments into a generator, so every call with `evaluate=False` was affected, including plain `And(x > 1, y > 2, evaluate=False)`.
The entry says the arguments were 'lost', but `.args` was correct. Only the internal `_argset` was empty, which made methods like `atoms()` return wrong results.
The bug was a regression in the 1.15 release candidate and may never have appeared in a released version, so an entry may not be needed at all.

structured_output.rationale: The fix adds one line, `args = tuple(args)`, to the `evaluate=False` path of `LatticeOp.__new__`. Before it, a generator was used up building the object, so `_argset` ended up empty and `And(x>1, y>2, evaluate=False).atoms(Symbol)` returned an empty set. The pull request that introduced this bug was only in a 1.15 release candidate, so NO ENTRY is defensible under the guide's rule about documenting only changes since the previous release. It also says the arguments were lost, when `.args` was fine and only internal state used by `atoms()` was wrong.
